facts.text: West Lebanon got its name in 1869 when the town was incorporated, likely honoring the Boone County Lebanon that opened a post office just eleven days earlier.
When the Wabash Railroad line opened a mile north of town in 1856, most residents moved closer to the station, reshaping West Lebanon.
West Lebanon still operates its Carnegie Library, built in 1916, a historic touchstone in the town’s downtown.
Every year the last weekend of September, West Lebanon hosts the Patriot Festival, celebrating its high school mascot Seeger High School.
West Lebanon sits just south of State Road 28, about 7.5 miles east of the Illinois border and five miles west of Williamsport.
Agriculture shapes West Lebanon’s landscape, dictating seasonal rhythms and fostering a calm, purposeful pace of local life.
